voice: The narration, one segment per scene. `est` is the length in seconds used until the voice has been generated; `pad` is the silence left after the segment.

segments.text: A lobster grows by leaving its shell behind. That shell is called an exuvia.
Exuvia is a data workbench, where the graph is the interface.
Each node is a plain Python or SQL file. Its inputs are just function parameters and table names, so the graph draws itself.
Edit a node, run it, and see the data. Only what's stale runs again, and every output is kept: cached, and content-addressed.
Put any node on its own schedule. When its output changes, everything downstream follows.
And you're not working alone. An AI agent reads, writes, runs and debugs nodes, right on the canvas, with the same tools you have.
Use the built-in agent, or bring Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, over MCP.
Views turn outputs into custom interfaces: React files that only read, with no back end to write.
Every version of the code is kept, and every output knows exactly which code produced it.
Start on your laptop with one command. Move to a hub when the team shows up.
Exuvia. Every run leaves a shell you can go back to.
